history.period: 1800s (one of the oldest Hindu temples in Nagaland; weakly sourced - verify)
history.summary: Gorkha Singhadevi Mandir at Upper Chandmari, Kohima, is a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Singhadevi, built by the Gorkhas of Northeast India and reported (by a travel blog, weakly sourced - verify) to date back to the 1800s, making it one of the oldest Hindu temples in Nagaland. The Gorkha community in Nagaland dates its settlement to 1833, per the Gorkha Public Panchayat Kohima president (nagalandpost, 2026). The temple is the community's central place of worship; Nagaland's Governor visited it in 2026, viewing an exhibition of historical photographs. Founding date and early history are not documented in reliable sources - the 1800s claim should be treated as unverified.

name: Gorkha Singhadevi Mandir
town_description: Kohima is the capital of Nagaland, set at about 1,444 m in the Naga Hills. It is known for the Kohima War Cemetery of the Second World War, the Hornbill Festival held at Kisama each December, and its strong Angami Naga cultural identity. The city is the state's administrative and cultural hub.

travel.road: On PWD Road at Chandmari/Upper Chandmari, ~1 km from Kohima town centre; local taxis and shared vehicles (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to May; December for the Hornbill Festival (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: 8:30 AM to 10:00 PM per a directory listing (verify).
